title: In-flight compaction race causing KV cache memory amplification
creator: Aisha Rahman
summary: A production incident on 2025-09-11 exposed a race between the KV cache compaction workers and live readers that temporarily amplified memory usage by retaining duplicate slab allocations and stalled evictions. The net effect was a 3x increase in cached memory across several hosts, degraded tail latency for inference requests, and automated node drains for capacity stabilization. This ticket captures the root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and a prioritized list of follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

root_cause_summary: A concurrency bug in the compaction path allowed two compaction workers to simultaneously rewrite the same slab region while readers continued to hold references. The rewritten entries were temporarily inserted as new slab allocations without properly transferring reference counts from the old entries; old entries could not be freed because readers held epoch-stamped references. Because eviction scoring deferred on items involved in recent compaction, both old and new entries remained resident, producing short-lived duplication of roughly 2x–3x the expected memory footprint. Under sustained write-heavy workloads this led to eviction pressure cascading into latency spikes and autoscaler churn.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start KV cache with compaction worker concurrency set to >=2 and eviction delay configured to 500ms.
2) Produce a synthetic workload that writes high cardinality prefixes with frequent updates (50k unique prefixes/minute) and short TTLs.
3) Force compaction schedule to run on overlapping slab ranges by decreasing compaction window to 2s and seeding clock jitter between workers.
4) Observe slab allocator metrics: duplicate allocation counts rise and eviction_pressure_gauge increases; live readers hold epoch references preventing free.
5) Capture logs from compaction workers showing concurrent rewrite of same slab IDs and missing atomic handoff of refcounts.
Notes: an integration harness and variant of this repro already implemented in kvcache/integration/tests/compaction_race_test.go (internal repo link in 'links').
mitigations_taken: Short-term: temporarily disable concurrent compaction (set compactor.max_parallel=1) across affected clusters.
Short-term: lower compaction frequency and reduce compaction window to avoid overlap during peak write periods.
Short-term: tightened eviction aggressiveness for the small-req path to reclaim duplicated slabs faster (evict.score_decay set from 0.6 to 0.4).
Operational: added oncall runbook steps to disable compaction concurrency and roll compactor config via canary before full rollout.
Communication: incident postmortem shared with SRE and Product; customers with SLA impacted were notified per the incident policy.
long_term_remediation: 1) Implement atomic compaction handoff: compaction must perform rewrite and then atomically swap the pointer under compaction lock, transferring refcounts to new entries before releasing old references.

2) Introduce compaction sequencing token: assign each compaction pass a monotonic sequence and make eviction logic treat entries touched by in-flight compactions as eligible for expedited reclamation if a newer sequence supersedes them.
3) Harden reference counting: convert soft refcount updates in the slab allocator to atomic 64-bit operations and add assertive vsan sanity checks in debug builds.
4) Add backpressure: when compaction throughput cannot keep up, throttle writers at the cache ingress to avoid amplification during re-writes.
5) Expand test coverage: add deterministic, thread-sanitized unit/integration tests that simulate compaction concurrency with epoch-based readers and verify no transient duplication.
6) Scheduler improvement: improve compactor worker placement so workers avoid operating on adjacent slab ranges concurrently (range partitioning).
7) Observability: emit new metrics (compaction.inflight_count, compaction.overlap_detected, slab.duplicate_allocs) and add alert thresholds for overlap_detected > 0.
8) Release changes behind a runtime flag and perform staged rollout with ramped canaries + memory health gating.

notes: This incident differs from previous KV cache incidents in that the symptom was transient memory amplification due to duplication rather than a persistent leak or metadata corruption. Many prior tickets focused on eviction heuristics and tombstone accumulation; this one requires a correctness fix in the compaction handoff plus improvements to scheduling and observability. We plan to include the compaction handoff fix in runtime-1.20.1 and run a staged rollout with memory health gates. Post-release, we will run a 72-hour soak with a synthetic heavy-update workload to validate the fix under production-like churn.
